title: What we've learned scaling AI coding agents at Spotify
excerpt: How Spotify built Xirp, a vendor-neutral agentic development environment, and why pairing it with Portal turns organizational context into a multiplier for every agent session.
content_html:
How Spotify built Xirp, a vendor-neutral agentic development environment, and why pairing it with Portal turns organizational context into a multiplier for every agent session.

Every CTO I speak with has moved past the adoption question. Their engineering organizations are using AI coding agents daily. But the landscape beneath them is in constant motion with new models, new agents, rising costs, pricing structures that shift quarter to quarter, and capabilities that advance overnight.

The real challenge is no longer velocity alone. It is ensuring teams have the flexibility to adopt whatever maximizes value at any given moment, without accumulating vendor dependency or compounding costs as you scale.

At Spotify, with thousands of engineers operating across hundreds of teams, this tension defines how we approach our development infrastructure. Our engineers require the autonomy to adopt the best available tool for their work, and what qualifies as best evolves rapidly. But autonomy without structure produces fragmentation, duplicated effort, and inconsistent outcomes. Reconciling that tension is what has driven our approach.

From one agent to thousands of sessions

The progression was predictable in hindsight. Teams began with a single agent. One session, one developer, one task. Then adoption accelerated.

Engineers, and later on non-engineers, started orchestrating multiple agents in parallel, across different sessions and tools, repositories, and branches. Context accumulated in one session but was needed in another. Institutional knowledge fragmented into individual configurations — CLAUDE.md files, bespoke MCP setups, personal prompt libraries — making it harder to carry that context across teams and workflows.

The resulting entropy impacted productivity. PRs increased, but so did rework, inconsistency, and wasted tokens. Agents in one session would expend cycles rediscovering what another session had already resolved.

Moreover, engineers were investing as much effort reconstructing context as they were on building new capabilities. And at the organizational level, creating greater visibility across thousands of concurrent sessions became an increasingly important priority.

This was not a new class of problem for us. A decade ago, the complexity of thousands of engineers operating across thousands of services produced the same category of fragmentation. That is why we built Backstage, a unified, structured source of truth for how our systems interconnect: dependency maps, component metadata, ownership, architectural decisions. Backstage became the foundation of our internal developer platform, and we subsequently built Portal, so any organization can get the same benefits without managing the infrastructure themselves.

AI coding agents have introduced an entirely new dimension of that same organizational complexity. It requires its own solution.

Enter Xirp

Xirp is a vendor-neutral agentic development environment born out of a concrete engineering need.

Xirp was built to help our developers manage dozens of concurrent agent sessions across multiple harnesses (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, etc.), making it tenable to coordinate 50+ parallel sessions. Every session operates in its own worktree, enabling dozens of agents to work concurrently on the same codebase without interference. Context is decoupled from any single agent or harness; switch tools mid-project, and the full working state carries over. Vendor neutrality is an architectural requirement that emerged directly from how our engineers work.

From a strategic perspective, this is precisely the capability needed across our organization: the freedom to leverage the best available tool at any given moment, without incurring a migration cost every time the ecosystem evolves. Xirp lets our engineers switch models mid-task and route every job to the best available price performance, including open source models that we host ourselves, so that we are never locked in.

When a new model emerges, our engineers transition without reconstructing their environment. They are able to move fluidly between coding agents, preserve context across sessions, and orchestrate parallel workstreams.

We're seeing good validation internally: thousands of Spotify engineers have organically adopted Xirp across more than 36,000 sessions, resulting in faster context switching and cost efficiencies.

Xirp + Portal: the multiplier effect

Xirp on its own addresses the multi-agent orchestration challenge, and when paired with Portal, it becomes a true agent command center.

When Xirp connects to Portal, every agent session initializes with organizational context drawn from your software catalog: component architecture, dependency graphs, ownership topology, and the architectural decisions that govern how systems interrelate.

The result is a shared institutional baseline your entire engineering organization operates from. The same structured knowledge that made Backstage transformative for human engineers now makes AI agents dramatically more effective.

The value compounds in both directions. After each session, transcripts and metadata flow back into Portal, providing comprehensive visibility across the organization: what has been accomplished, who is working on what, and where to resume. Any engineer or agent can pick up where another left off, because the full working context is preserved in Portal.

Work becomes interchangeable across the team. Duplicate effort is eliminated. The institutional knowledge that one engineer's agent session produces becomes immediately available to every subsequent session across the team.

Consider the skills, rules, plugins, and MCP configurations that every team develops independently. Portal consolidates it into a curated marketplace where teams contribute, discover, and build upon each other's work. For teams that prefer to operate directly within their agent of choice, Portal's MCP tools surface the same organizational context natively within any coding session.

Build, experiment, and ship like Spotify

Spotify's engineering culture was built on a conviction: give teams the autonomy to move fast, but invest in the shared infrastructure that makes that speed sustainable. We applied that principle to developer experience with Backstage and Portal, to product development with Confidence, our experimentation platform, and now to agentic software development with Xirp and Portal.

The organizations that learn fastest, that compound their engineering knowledge into shared, structured systems rather than leaving it scattered across individuals, will be the ones that capture the full value of AI-assisted development. We have proven that pattern at scale. Now we're shipping that expertise to you.

Xirp delivers value as a standalone agentic development environment today. Connect it to Portal, and organizational context becomes the multiplier, compounding the effectiveness of every agent, every session, every team.

To learn more or try it for free, visit xirp.spotify.com.

content_html_zh:
Spotify 如何构建 Xirp（一个供应商中立的代理开发环境），以及为什么将其与 Portal 配对可以将组织环境变成每个代理会话的倍增器。

与我交谈过的每一位 CTO 都已经摆脱了采用问题。 他们的工程组织每天都在使用人工智能编码代理。 但它们背后的格局不断变化，新模式、新代理商、不断上升的成本、逐季变化的定价结构以及一夜之间进步的能力。

真正的挑战不再仅仅是速度。 它确保团队能够在任何给定时刻灵活地采用任何可以实现价值最大化的方法，而不会随着规模的扩大而积累供应商依赖性或复合成本。

在 Spotify，数百个团队中有数千名工程师，这种紧张关系决定了我们如何处理我们的开发基础设施。 我们的工程师需要自主地采用最好的可用工具来完成他们的工作，而最好的工具正在迅速发展。 但没有结构的自治会产生碎片化、重复工作和不一致的结果。 调和这种紧张关系是我们采取行动的动力。

从一名代理到数千次会话

事后看来，进展是可以预见的。 团队从一名代理人开始。 一场会议，一名开发人员，一项任务。 然后采用速度加快。

工程师，以及后来的非工程师，开始跨不同的会话和工具、存储库和分支并行编排多个代理。 上下文在一个会话中积累，但在另一会话中需要。 机构知识分散为单独的配置 - CLAUDE.md 文件、定制的 MCP 设置、个人提示库 - 使得跨团队和工作流程携带该上下文变得更加困难。

由此产生的熵影响了生产力。 PR 增加了，但返工、不一致和浪费的代币也增加了。 一个会话中的代理将花费周期重新发现另一会话已经解决的问题。

此外，工程师在重建环境方面所投入的精力与构建新功能所投入的精力一样多。 在组织层面，在数千个并发会话中创建更大的可见性成为越来越重要的优先事项。

这对我们来说并不是一个新问题。 十年前，数千名工程师在数千项服务中操作的复杂性产生了同样类别的碎片化。 这就是我们构建 Backstage 的原因，这是一个统一的、结构化的事实来源，用于说明我们的系统如何互连：依赖关系图、组件元数据、所有权、架构决策。 Backstage成为我们内部开发者平台的基础，我们随后构建了Portal，因此任何组织都可以获得相同的好处，而无需自己管理基础设施。

人工智能编码代理引入了同样组织复杂性的全新维度。 它需要自己的解决方案。

输入西普

Xirp 是一个供应商中立的代理开发环境，诞生于具体的工程需求。

Xirp 旨在帮助我们的开发人员跨多个工具（Claude Code、Gemini CLI、Codex 等）管理数十个并发代理会话，使其能够协调 50 多个并行会话。 每个会话都在自己的工作树中运行，使数十个代理能够在同一代码库上同时工作而不会相互干扰。 上下文与任何单个代理或工具分离；在项目中切换工具，完整的工作状态将继续。 供应商中立性是一项架构要求，直接源于我们工程师的工作方式。

从战略角度来看，这正是我们整个组织所需的能力：在任何特定时刻自由地利用最佳可用工具，而不会在每次生态系统发展时产生迁移成本。 Xirp 让我们的工程师在任务中切换模型，并将每项工作安排到最佳的可用性价比，包括我们自己托管的开源模型，这样我们就不会被锁定。

当新模型出现时，我们的工程师会在不重建环境的情况下进行过渡。 他们能够在编码代理之间流畅地移动，跨会话保留上下文，并协调并行工作流。

我们在内部看到了良好的验证：数千名 Spotify 工程师在超过 36,000 个会话中有机地采用了 Xirp，从而实现了更快的上下文切换和成本效率。

Xirp + Portal：乘数效应

Xirp 本身解决了多代理编排挑战，当与 Portal 配合使用时，它成为真正的代理指挥中心。

当 Xirp 连接到 Portal 时，每个代理会话都会使用从软件目录中提取的组织上下文进行初始化：组件架构、依赖关系图、所有权拓扑以及控制系统如何相互关联的架构决策。

其结果是整个工程组织的运作都遵循一个共享的机构基线。 使 Backstage 为人类工程师带来变革的结构化知识现在使人工智能代理的效率显着提高。

该值在两个方向上复合。 每次会议结束后，记录和元数据都会流回到 Portal，从而提供整个组织的全面可见性：已完成什么、谁正在做什么以及在哪里恢复。 任何工程师或代理都可以从其他人留下的地方继续，因为完整的工作上下文都保存在 Portal 中。

整个团队的工作可以互换。 消除了重复的工作。 一名工程师的代理会议产生的机构知识可以立即供团队中的每个后续会议使用。

考虑每个团队独立开发的技能、规则、插件和 MCP 配置。 Portal 将其整合为一个精心策划的市场，团队可以在其中贡献、发现并构建彼此的工作。 对于喜欢直接在其选择的代理中进行操作的团队来说，Portal 的 MCP 工具可以在任何编码会话中呈现相同的组织上下文。

像 Spotify 一样构建、实验和发布

Spotify 的工程文化建立在这样一个信念之上：赋予团队快速行动的自主权，但投资于共享基础设施，使这种速度可持续。 我们将这一原则应用于 Backstage 和 Portal 的开发人员体验、我们的实验平台 Confidence 的产品开发，以及现在 Xirp 和 Portal 的代理软件开发。

那些学习速度最快的组织，将其工程知识整合到共享的结构化系统中，而不是将其分散在个人中，将能够充分发挥人工智能辅助开发的价值。 我们已经大规模证明了这种模式。 现在我们正在向您提供专业知识。

如今，Xirp 作为独立的代理开发环境提供价值。 将其连接到门户，组织环境将成为倍增器，提高每个代理、每个会话、每个团队的效率。

要了解更多信息或免费试用，请访问 xirp.spotify.com。
